territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Negative prompts trigger boundary-following exclusion along nearest contrast edges rather than semantic removal, producing over-carving in textured or cluttered regions.

territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The ranking among SAM's candidate masks for ambiguous clicks matches the relative frequency of comparable mask granularities in SA-1B, and stays fixed even when image evidence (contrast, closure) is manipulated to favor the alternative.

territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The decoder's output token embeddings (after cross-attention with image features) carry linearly decodable category information well above what the raw pooled image features at the same location provide.

territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For target domains where oracle prompt/multimask selection already achieves high IoU (gap = wrong default granularity/convention), learning a small set of soft prompt tokens closes most of the gap; LoRA's extra capacity only matters when oracle-prompt IoU is low (gap = appearance).

title: Mask instability under click jitter predicts SAM errors better than SAM's own IoU-prediction head.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The variance of predicted masks under small prompt perturbations (click jitter within the object) is a strictly better failure detector than the IoU head, especially out of domain, because it measures decision-boundary proximity rather than a learned regression that can itself shift.

title: Everything-mode grid prompting has a computable blind spot: objects thinner than the grid pitch are missed at rates predicted by pure geometry.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Everything-mode recall for an object is well predicted by the probability that a grid point lands inside it (a closed-form function of its area and shape), meaning the failure is a sampling artifact, not a perception failure.

territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The distribution of LoRA update energy across (layer depth x projection type) is a stable, interpretable signature: photometric/sensor shifts load early V/O; label-convention/granularity shifts load late Q/K and decoder cross-attention.

title: Learned LoRA updates have an effective rank that saturates far below the allocated rank, and that saturation value is a transferable 'intrinsic rank' of the task.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For SAM adaptation, the stable rank of the converged update B*A saturates as allocated rank grows, and the saturation value (a) predicts the minimal allocated rank achieving full accuracy, and (b) is consistent across LoRA variants and seeds - i.e., it is a property of the task, not the method.

territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] At low rank, the converged update subspace retains substantial overlap with the *initial* random subspace of A (it never fully rotates away), so different seeds converge to genuinely different functions - explaining why low-rank results have higher seed variance and why LoRA soups help.

territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] After LoRA adaptation of SAM to a new domain, the causal importance profile of attention heads (measured by ablation damage) is nearly unchanged - adaptation amplifies/reweights existing pathways rather than creating new ones.

core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Modality shifts are overwhelmingly a first-layer problem: once token statistics are renormalized to natural-image-like distributions, frozen deeper layers process the new modality adequately.

territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For photometric/stain/sensor-gain shifts, tuning only LayerNorm scales and biases (a few thousand parameters) recovers most of LoRA's gain, because these shifts manifest as channel-wise mean/variance displacement of features.

title: Label-convention gaps do NOT live in the decoder: decoder-only LoRA fails to absorb label-style shifts that encoder LoRA absorbs easily.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Convention changes (e.g., include-holes vs exclude-holes, instance vs semantic grouping) require encoder feature changes because grouping evidence is computed in the encoder; the decoder is a readout too weak to re-group.

territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Projecting gradients through a low-rank bottleneck suppresses high-variance conflicting components, raising per-batch gradient cosine similarity; PEFT's optimization stability is a variance-reduction effect, not a capacity effect.

territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Overfitting attributed to high rank is caused by unregularized singular-value growth; with nuclear-norm or spectral weight decay on B*A, high-rank LoRA weakly dominates low-rank across data scales (it can always emulate low rank).

territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The number of significant components in the frozen-feature discrepancy between source-like and target data (e.g., eigen-spectrum of the mean-shift + covariance-mismatch operator per layer) linearly predicts the minimal LoRA rank achieving near-max accuracy.

core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Additive merging of two domain LoRAs preserves both domains' performance iff their update subspaces are near-orthogonal per layer; the performance drop under merging is a monotone function of a single overlap statistic computable without any evaluation data.

territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Single-domain fine-tuning (which usually has one 'correct' granularity) collapses multimask diversity globally, not just in-domain: mean pairwise IoU among the three outputs rises sharply everywhere, destroying part/whole option coverage.

territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The IoU head's calibration (error of predicted vs actual IoU) on source-domain data degrades much faster during PEFT than source-domain mask IoU itself - self-knowledge is the most fragile capability.

territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Forgetting is concentrated on source categories whose frozen-feature statistics are CLOSEST to the target domain (they share the pathways being rewritten), contradicting the intuition that 'far' capabilities are unaffected and 'near' ones benefit.

territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Boundary precision and region correctness are stored separably: fine-tuning on coarse labels selectively overwrites the boundary-precision store (hypothesized to live in the upsampling path and early decoder), degrading boundary-F on ALL domains while region IoU is unaffected.

title: PEFT forgetting is displacement, not erasure: 50 rehearsal images restore most zero-shot loss, implying the knowledge is intact but de-routed.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] After domain LoRA, a tiny rehearsal phase (tens of generic images with diverse prompts, few steps, adapter-only updates) recovers the majority of zero-shot degradation while keeping target-domain gains - indicating shallow displacement.

title: Single-prompt fine-tuning kills multi-click repair: adapted SAM loses the ability to integrate correction clicks even in its new specialty domain.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM's ability to use 2nd..kth corrective clicks is a distinct skill maintained only if training includes iterative prompts; single-prompt fine-tuning degrades click-integration so much that in-domain interactive performance of the adapted model falls below the un-adapted base after 3+ clicks.

title: Adaptation makes SAM texture-greedy: fine-tuning on homogeneous-texture domains measurably shifts SAM's shape-vs-texture reliance, predictable from target-set texture statistics.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] PEFT shifts SAM's grouping cues toward whatever cue-dimension has lowest variance in the target set (often texture in medical/industrial data), and the shift magnitude is predictable from a texture-homogeneity statistic of the training set.

title: 'LoRA learns less but forgets less' has a crossover: when the required update is high-rank, LoRA both underfits the target AND forgets more per unit of target gain than full fine-tuning.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Forgetting-per-target-gain is the right exchange rate, and LoRA's advantage on it inverts for target domains requiring high-rank updates: forced through a narrow subspace, LoRA overdrives shared directions, causing MORE collateral damage per point of target improvement.

title: Calibration forgetting has a one-hour fix nobody applies: retraining only the IoU head post-adaptation restores self-assessment without touching masks.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Post-hoc IoU-head-only retraining (frozen everything else) on a few hundred target masks restores calibration to near-base levels for both target and source, because the head's inputs still contain sufficient quality-relevant signal - miscalibration is a readout mismatch, not information loss.

title: SAM segments photometric contiguity, not objects: it has no amodal completion even when occlusion is trivially inferable, and this is quantifiable as a core defect.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM's masks are governed by photometric contiguity: for objects split by thin occluders, SAM returns the visible fragment containing the click at rates near 100%, regardless of how visually obvious the completion is, and no prompt strategy recovers the full object reliably.

title: SAM hallucinates boundaries where contrast vanishes by snapping to the nearest strong edge - a predictable 'closed contour at any cost' prior.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] In contrast-gap regions SAM does not interpolate smoothly (human-like completion) but snaps to the nearest strong irrelevant edge, with snap probability governed by edge strength and distance - making its hallucinations systematic and predictable by a simple local edge-field model.

title: SAM's thin-structure failure is tokenization-limited, not knowledge-limited: failure onset sits at a fixed fraction of patch size and is cured by input upsampling, not by fine-tuning.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] There is a critical structure width, a fixed fraction of the 16px patch size, below which SAM fails regardless of domain familiarity - and above which it succeeds even zero-shot on unfamiliar domains; simple input upsampling shifts the failure point exactly as geometry predicts, while LoRA fine-tuning at native resolution does not shift it.

title: SAM learned an annotator, not nature: its output mask morphology (curvature spectra, corner statistics) matches SA-1B's machine-annotation style and differs measurably from human tracing.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM outputs have a characteristic boundary-morphology signature (smoothness, curvature distribution, vertex/corner statistics) inherited from SA-1B's generation process, distinguishable from human-annotated morphology by a simple classifier even at matched accuracy.

title: SAM has a contrast-polarity bias: at matched contrast magnitude, dark-object-on-light-ground and light-object-on-dark-ground are not segmented equally well.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM performs systematically better on one contrast polarity (predicted: dark-on-light, reflecting photographic shadow/object statistics), with a gap that persists across shapes and scales and largely explains zero-shot deficits on polarity-inverted modalities.

title: SAM degrades much faster under high-frequency noise than under blur at matched distortion level, exposing edge-dependence over region-statistics grouping.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM's grouping relies dominantly on high-frequency edge evidence rather than region statistics: additive HF noise (which corrupts edges but preserves region means) will damage IoU far more than blur (which destroys HF but preserves large-scale region structure) at matched PSNR/SSIM.

title: SAM's transparency failure is inherited annotation convention, not perceptual limitation: it segments what SA-1B annotators outlined, and flips behavior when prompted at annotation-convention boundaries.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For transparent objects, SA-1B labels mix conventions (sometimes the surface, sometimes the background seen through it); SAM internalized this mixture, so its transparency behavior is high-variance convention sampling rather than low-quality perception - and its multimask candidates often contain BOTH readings.

title: SAM binds attached shadows into object masks at a systematic, illumination-dependent rate - an unaudited labeling ambiguity every SAM-labeled dataset inherits.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM includes attached shadows at a stable rate that varies with shadow contrast and attachment geometry (predictable), rather than randomly - constituting a measurable convention with parameters, which downstream datasets absorb invisibly.

title: SAM failure is predictable before prompting: a linear probe on encoder features forecasts achievable IoU, revealing a 'segmentability' direction in feature space.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The encoder embedding contains a low-dimensional 'segmentability' signal: a linear readout on pooled/regional features predicts oracle-prompt achievable IoU with useful accuracy, before any prompting - implying failure is determined at encoding time, not decoding time.

title: SAM is brittle on very large objects: masks degrade when objects exceed the relative-size range common in SA-1B, and simple crop-and-zoom-out inference fixes it.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM's quality drops systematically for objects above a relative-area threshold (a rarely-populated regime in web-photo mask statistics), with failure modes of under-segmentation into parts; padding the image to shrink relative object size restores quality - a pure dataset-prior failure.

title: The medical-SAM gap lives mostly downstream of the encoder: frozen encoder + retrained lightweight decoder recovers the bulk of full fine-tuning, because encoder features already separate anatomy.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM's frozen encoder features linearly separate most medical structure boundaries; the dominant gap is decoder/prompt-space mismatch (what to select, which granularity), so decoder-side retraining captures the majority of achievable gain on most medical 2D tasks.

title: Label conventions are portable modules: a decoder retrained on convention A over a frozen encoder transfers that convention to unseen domains without further training.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A decoder retrained to implement a convention (e.g., 'always semantic-part granularity' or 'exclude holes') on dataset X will apply that convention zero-shot on unseen datasets Y, because conventions are readout policies over encoder-general features.

title: Per-layer feature-shift profiles prescribe PEFT placement: the depth at which source-target CKA collapses predicts which layers need adapters, per domain.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The layer-resolved divergence profile between target-domain features and natural-image features (CKA or subspace angle per layer, computable with unlabeled data) predicts the placement that maximizes adaptation efficiency: adapters placed at and after the divergence onset match full placement; earlier-only placement fails when divergence onsets late.

title: SAM's decoder allocates constant compute per object regardless of boundary complexity; its error scales with contour information content - a measurable compute-starvation law.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Boundary error per unit contour length grows with contour complexity (curvature entropy) under fixed decoder compute, and recursive self-prompting on error-dense sub-regions (giving the same decoder more passes) recovers accuracy - demonstrating starvation, not ignorance.

title: Oracle decomposition of SAM's boundary error: feeding ground-truth low-res masks through the upsampling path measures exactly how much error is decoder-intrinsic vs upsampling-intrinsic.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A large, quantifiable share of fine-boundary error is introduced after the decoder's decision - in the low-res mask representation and fixed upsampling - such that oracle low-res masks passed through SAM's own output path already lose most of the boundary-F headroom that fine-tuning papers chase.

title: SAM's IoU head is a domain-difficulty meter, not an instance-quality meter: it ranks datasets well but barely ranks instances within an image.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Most of the IoU head's correlation with true quality comes from coarse difficulty factors (domain, image quality, object size) - within-image, across candidate masks of comparable size, its instance-level resolution is near chance, making it unfit for its primary use case (picking the best mask).

territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Target IoU vs number of labeled images under fixed LoRA follows a shifted power law whose exponent is (approximately) shared across domains for a fixed model/method; domains differ mainly in offset (zero-shot level) and asymptote.

core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because LoRA needs to observe the domain's feature-shift directions (not its full appearance diversity), a small set chosen to cover frozen-feature space supports adaptation as well as much larger random sets; marginal value of a labeled image is predicted by its feature-space distance to already-selected images.

core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Incoherent per-image boundary noise requires high-rank updates to memorize; low-rank LoRA is therefore implicitly robust, and there exists a predictable noise-level crossover where rank-4 outperforms rank-64 on clean-test IoU despite losing on train fit.

core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Under domain shift, the IoU head's errors are anti-correlated with true difficulty of the shift-specific failure modes: the model is most confidently wrong precisely on the patterns that define the domain gap, so confidence-filtered self-training reinforces base-model biases and cannot learn the gap.

core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For LoRA on SAM, images where zero-shot already succeeds contribute negligible learning signal; front-loading high-error images (anti-curriculum by zero-shot IoU) reaches target performance in fewer steps and, in the few-shot regime, selecting ONLY hard images beats matched random selection - inverting classic curriculum advice.

core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] LoRA has enough capacity to memorize patient-level appearance; image-level splits therefore overstate generalization, and the inflation grows with rank and shrinks with patient count - making some published few-shot rankings between PEFT methods artifacts of differential memorization.

territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Style-space augmentation (histogram/stain/noise transforms sampled around the target distribution) reduces the rank needed for a given accuracy by a quantifiable factor, because augmentation removes nuisance directions from the required update, shrinking its intrinsic rank (link to W15-B001-A-012).

core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Instances with high multimask disagreement carry more adaptation-relevant information per label (they localize convention/granularity uncertainty, which is what adaptation must resolve) than low-confidence instances (which mix noise, difficulty, and out-of-scope junk); disagreement-based acquisition yields faster IoU gains per label.

core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM's multimask spread was trained on exactly the ambiguity structure that drives human disagreement (one click, many valid masks), so its spread metrics predict inter-annotator IoU variance on the same instances - making SAM a cheap simulator of annotation ambiguity.

core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The IoU head fails in a systematically optimistic direction under shift, and the magnitude of optimism (estimable with few labels, or label-free via jitter-agreement as ground-truth proxy) is a monotone, roughly domain-rankable function of true zero-shot performance drop.

territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For pipeline-level outcomes (auto-label precision at fixed recall, human-routing efficiency), recalibrating the uncertainty pathway on the target domain (IoU head + a small feature adapter feeding it) achieves a large fraction of the value of full LoRA adaptation at a tiny fraction of the risk (zero mask-behavior change, zero forgetting).

title: Ambiguity is conserved under adaptation: images ambiguous for zero-shot SAM remain ambiguous after LoRA fine-tuning - the ambiguity lives in the data, not the weights.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Per-instance ambiguity rankings (multimask spread, jitter variance) are highly rank-correlated before vs after adaptation, even as absolute accuracy improves - because ambiguity reflects stimulus properties (weak evidence, valid alternatives) that no in-distribution training removes.

territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Multimask spread (same input, alternative interpretations) tracks aleatoric/stimulus ambiguity, while jitter variance (perturbed input, same interpretation) tracks epistemic/model uncertainty; in-domain they correlate, out-of-domain they dissociate (jitter rises, spread doesn't), enabling a practical two-dimensional uncertainty readout from one model.

title: SAM's runner-up masks audit datasets: when the top mask disagrees with ground truth but a runner-up matches it, the dataset likely has a systematic label-convention offset.

core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The signature [top-1 wrong, runner-up right] is diagnostic: at instance level it flags label errors; when its rate is elevated dataset-wide with consistent direction (e.g., GT always matches the larger candidate), it reveals convention offsets (holes, granularity) - separable from random noise by directional consistency.

core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A standardized prompt-budget curve (1..k points, box, box+points, best-of-multimask) will show that a large share of published 'SAM fails on domain X' gaps closes at modest prompt budgets - reattributing many failures from representation to interface, and revealing which domain failures are real.

territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Fine-tuned models learn to exploit tight-box statistics (box edge = mask boundary within noise), converting the evaluation prompt into a supervisory leak; zero-shot SAM exploits it less; hence box-prompt evaluations systematically overstate adaptation gains, and the overstatement grows with training-protocol/evaluation-protocol match.

title: The missing null baseline: frozen-SAM-encoder + linear/shallow head matches published PEFT methods on a nontrivial fraction of adaptation benchmarks.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] On a meaningful fraction of standard adaptation benchmarks, a probing-class baseline (frozen encoder, shallow convolutional or linear decode head trained on target data) lands within 1-2 IoU of published PEFT numbers - implying those benchmarks measure feature readout, not adaptation, and are uninformative for comparing adaptation methods.

title: PEFT gains partially reduce to training-time gains: at matched wall-clock optimization budget, method differences shrink because 'efficient' methods simply take more well-tuned steps.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A visible share of reported inter-method differences in SAM adaptation disappears under matched-compute protocols (equal GPU-seconds including forward/backward cost differences), and the survivor differences concentrate in methods with genuinely different inductive biases (placement, normalization) rather than reparameterizations.

title: The SAM-adaptation benchmark suite is effectively one benchmark: method rankings across popular datasets are so correlated that multi-dataset tables add almost no evidence.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Across published and reproduced results, between-dataset rank correlation of adaptation methods is very high within domain families (e.g., endoscopy sets, CT sets), such that the effective number of independent evaluations in a typical 8-dataset table is 2-3 - computable via ranking-correlation eigenanalysis.

title: The random-encoder control nobody runs: LoRA-adapting a frozen RANDOM-weight encoder quantifies how much of 'foundation model adaptation' is just any-features-plus-training.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] On simple adaptation domains (high-contrast, texture-separable), LoRA + decoder training over a frozen randomly-initialized encoder reaches a nontrivial fraction of pretrained-SAM adaptation performance, and the pretraining premium (pretrained minus random) varies enormously across benchmarks - exposing which benchmarks actually test foundation knowledge.

title: The foundation-model tax: on narrow, high-volume domains, a small from-scratch specialist beats LoRA-adapted SAM at matched TOTAL cost (labels + compute + inference).
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For domains that are narrow (low appearance diversity) and inference-heavy (deployment cost dominates), the total-cost frontier favors compact specialists once labeled data exceeds a threshold; the threshold is predictable from domain diversity measures - giving a decision rule for when NOT to use foundation models.

title: Averaging beats capacity: souping LoRAs from different seeds on the SAME task outperforms doubling rank - PEFT is variance-limited, not capacity-limited.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] In common SAM adaptation regimes, weight-averaging k rank-r LoRAs (same data, different seeds) improves test IoU more than training one rank-kr LoRA at equal total compute, because the binding constraint is estimation variance, not expressivity.

title: LoRA updates are 1-bit compressible: keeping only per-parameter signs (with one learned scale per layer) preserves most adaptation - the knowledge is in directions, not magnitudes.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Binarizing converged LoRA factors (sign x per-layer scale) retains the large majority of target-domain performance, indicating the update's functional content is directional and low-precision - and predicting that magnitude-focused regularizers and optimizers are tuning noise.

title: PEFT's gains arrive almost immediately: most target-domain improvement happens in the first few percent of training steps, and the long tail mainly moves calibration and boundary polish - three separable timescales.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM adaptation exhibits distinct timescales: (1) region-level IoU jumps within the first ~5% of steps (convention acquisition), (2) boundary-F improves slowly and linearly, (3) calibration drifts continuously and can worsen late - implying early stopping at timescale-1 completion plus post-hoc head recalibration dominates the standard recipe.

title: Adaptation without touching the model: a learned 3x3-conv (or LUT) input transformation matches low-rank LoRA on sensor-shift domains - the entire 'domain gap' passes through the lens.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For sensor/photometric shifts, a tiny learned input-space transform (per-domain color LUT or single conv layer, trained with SAM frozen end-to-end through it) achieves parity with rank-4-8 LoRA - and its learned parameters are interpretable (revealing WHAT the shift physically is).

title: Adaptation by subtraction: learning to GATE (mask out) a small set of encoder channels - adding zero new parameters of representation - recovers much of the domain gap, because shift acts as feature interference.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A learned binary/soft gate over encoder channels (hundreds of parameters) recovers a substantial fraction of LoRA's gains on many domains, because out-of-domain inputs excite feature detectors whose downstream effect is destructive interference rather than missing information.

title: Scale-shifted domains (satellite, microscopy) are adaptable through positional encodings alone: retuning PE frequencies fixes what looks like a semantic gap.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A meaningful share of the zero-shot gap on scale-atypical domains is caused by mismatch between the domain's spatial-structure statistics and the PE's learned/fixed frequency profile; adapting ONLY positional-encoding parameters (a tiny fraction of weights) recovers that share, while content-atypical domains gain nothing from PE tuning.

title: Label-free test-time adaptation via self-consistency: a few gradient steps minimizing disagreement across prompts/augmentations of ONE image improves that image's masks - SAM contains its own training signal.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Enforcing consistency (via a few LoRA-parameter gradient steps per image) among masks from jittered prompts, flipped inputs, and multimask candidates improves single-image quality on shifted domains, because inconsistency is enriched at exactly the model's error locations (per W15-B001-A-009's premise).
mutation_note: MUTATE. SAM + self-consistency test-time adaptation matches the established entropy/consistency-TTA family (method permutation). Salvage: the diagnostic claim that cross-prompt/augmentation inconsistency is spatially enriched at true error locations under shift; test that as a measurement (error-localization AUROC), with per-image adaptation demoted to a secondary intervention arm.

title: SAM's self-training ancestry left fingerprints: error modes are correlated across all SAM-derived models because SA-1B was partially machine-generated by earlier SAM versions - a monoculture defect.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Models trained on SA-1B (SAM variants, distilled/efficient SAMs, and fine-tuned derivatives) share error modes far beyond what architecture or scale predicts - their errors correlate more with each other than with models trained on human-only masks, because the annotation bootstrap propagated specific systematic omissions/conventions.

title: SAM carries a masks-per-image prior: everything-mode output counts regress toward SA-1B's per-image mask-count distribution regardless of true scene content.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] On synthetic scenes with controlled true object counts spanning 1 to thousands, SAM's everything-mode count deviates from truth systematically TOWARD the SA-1B per-image mask-count mode, beyond what grid/NMS mechanics (W15-B001-A-040) explain - i.e., a learned prior in the decoder/IoU-filtering, not just sampling mechanics.

title: 'Segment anything' has measurable anisotropy: zero-shot quality stratified by scene type maps SA-1B's content skew, quantifying WHERE the anything-claim fails before any domain-specific study.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Zero-shot performance across scene taxonomies (indoor/outdoor, aerial, document, industrial, scientific imaging, etc.) varies widely and correlates strongly with content-frequency estimates in SA-1B-like web-photo distributions - making 'domain gap' largely predictable from content frequency rather than intrinsic difficulty.

title: SAM inherited photographic curation: at matched scene content and difficulty, 'non-photogenic' captures (bad framing, defocus, clutter) segment worse than curated-style photos - an aesthetics bias in a geometry model.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Holding scene content constant, SAM performs measurably worse on uncurated-style captures than curated-style captures of the SAME scenes, beyond what image-quality metrics explain - because composition statistics (centering, lighting, depth-of-field conventions) are themselves features SAM's grouping relies on.

title: Active learning driven by SAM's IoU head selects convention conflicts, not model errors: the head's 'low quality' flags concentrate where target-domain labeling conventions differ from SA-1B's, wasting annotation budget.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] In convention-mismatched domains, low-predicted-IoU instances are enriched in convention disagreements (model produces an SA-1B-style valid mask that the target convention scores poorly) rather than perception failures; annotation budget spent there teaches the convention repeatedly instead of fixing errors - explaining observed inefficiency of confidence-based AL for SAM.

title: Privacy blurring in SA-1B taught SAM that blur boundaries are object boundaries: synthetic blur patches attract spurious masks at rates exceeding matched smooth regions.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because blurred regions in SA-1B co-occurred with maskable objects (faces, plates), SAM learned blur-transition edges as objectness evidence; it will therefore segment synthetic Gaussian-blur patches as objects at above-baseline rates, and be biased toward mask boundaries that follow blur transitions in natural defocus.

title: SA-1B is massively redundant for capability: models trained on well-chosen small fractions recover most zero-shot segmentation ability - measurable at reduced scale, with implications for what pretraining actually needs.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Capability saturates far below full scale under diversity-preserving subsampling: at compact model scale, training on a low-single-digit percent subset selected for scene/mask-statistics coverage recovers the large majority of full-subset-trained zero-shot performance, while random subsets need several times more data - implying capability lives in coverage, not count.

title: The ultrasound gap is mostly speckle, not anatomy: augmenting natural images with physically-modeled speckle noise closes a large share of SAM's ultrasound deficit without a single ultrasound image.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A LoRA trained ONLY on natural images corrupted with simulated speckle (multiplicative Rayleigh-family noise, no anatomy content) will transfer to real ultrasound and recover a large fraction of the gain achieved by training on real ultrasound - because the binding constraint is noise-statistics robustness, not anatomical knowledge.

title: Histopathology breaks SAM through scale-lessness, not appearance: without absolute-scale cues its granularity choice becomes unstable, and instability (not inaccuracy) is the measurable failure mode.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Pathology tiles lack the absolute-scale cues (familiar objects, perspective) that SAM implicitly uses for granularity selection; consequently, SAM's outputs on pathology are hypersensitive to zoom level and prompt position (unstable), even where per-prompt masks are locally plausible - instability is the primary defect, distinct from and larger than appearance-driven inaccuracy.

title: Geometry beats appearance in clutter: SAM segments rendered depth maps better than the corresponding RGB in dense scenes - though depth was near-absent from its training data.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For cluttered scenes, depth maps rendered as grayscale expose occlusion boundaries so cleanly that zero-shot SAM segments objects better from depth than from RGB - implying SAM's grouping is substantially a generic contour engine whose performance is input-representation-limited, not knowledge-limited, in clutter.

title: Structure supervises better than labels: adapting SAM to CT using ONLY inter-slice mask-consistency (no annotations) beats few-shot LoRA - volumetric coherence is a free supervisory signal labels can't match.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Enforcing prompt-propagated consistency between adjacent CT slices (segment slice i with a prompt, derive prompts for i+1 from the result, penalize incoherence) provides enough signal to adapt LoRA parameters label-free, and outperforms 10-20-image supervised LoRA - because it supplies thousands of weak constraints vs dozens of strong ones targeting exactly the model's instability modes.

title: SAM has an orientation prior from photography: rotation-sweep evaluation reveals anisotropic segmentation quality, and remote-sensing 'domain gap' partly dissolves under test-time rotation averaging.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SAM's quality on the same object varies systematically with its orientation (best at photo-canonical orientations); overhead imagery - which lacks canonical orientation - pays this anisotropy as a permanent tax that rotation-averaged inference (or PE-level fixes, W15-B001-A-083) largely removes without any training.

title: LoRAs die with their base model - but a cheap linear re-basing transform resurrects them: adapter knowledge is basis-specific yet linearly portable across model versions.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A domain LoRA's function can be transported to a new base model by learning a small linear map between the two models' feature spaces (fit on unlabeled generic images) and re-projecting the update - recovering a large fraction of adaptation quality without target-domain data, because the update encodes a feature-space displacement that survives linear re-expression.

title: Adaptation is path-dependent: fine-tuning A-then-B lands somewhere different from B-then-A even with identical final data exposure - sequential PEFT composes non-commutatively with predictable asymmetry.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Sequential LoRA adaptation (training one adapter through domains in sequence) is non-commutative: final joint performance depends on order, with a predictable rule - adapting from broad/diverse domains toward narrow ones preserves more joint capability than the reverse, because narrow-first commits shared directions to domain-specific uses (relates to W15-B001-A-031's capacity pressure).

title: Domain routing is already solved inside the frozen encoder: nearest-centroid gating on SAM features routes multi-domain traffic to the right LoRA as accurately as oracle domain labels - deployment needs no trained router.
territory: T01 SAM / Foundation Model adaptation / PEFT
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Domain identity is so linearly separable in frozen SAM encoder features that a training-free router (nearest domain-centroid, centroids from ~20 unlabeled images each) matches oracle-label routing end-to-end, and its distance-to-nearest-centroid doubles as a calibrated novel-domain detector triggering fallback to zero-shot mode.
mutation_note: MUTATE. 'Frozen features separate domains' is a widely assumed premise and nearest-centroid routing is engineering assembly. Salvage: rewrite around the only non-obvious content - the failure boundary on near-duplicate domains (e.g. two CT sites) and whether centroid distance is a calibrated novel-domain detector.

title: For mature organ benchmarks, the residual model-vs-reference gap is annotation protocol disagreement, not model error.
core_hypothesis: On well-benchmarked large organs, top models already sit inside the inter-rater disagreement band; the residual gap measures protocol ambiguity rather than model deficiency.

title: Boundary label noise in 3D medical data is anisotropic and systematic because annotators trace in-plane, and models inherit a slice-direction-dependent boundary bias.
core_hypothesis: Out-of-plane (through-slice) boundary labels are systematically biased and noisier than in-plane boundaries, and trained models reproduce this anisotropic error pattern.

title: Annotator identity is decodable from masks alone, and annotator-style normalization improves cross-dataset transfer more than image harmonization.
core_hypothesis: Each annotator or annotating institution has a stable, learnable contouring style (margin tightness, smoothing, inclusion rules), and this style is a first-order component of cross-dataset performance gaps.

title: Many 3D reference masks are sparse-slice annotations completed by interpolation, and models trained on them learn interpolation artifacts as anatomy.
core_hypothesis: Models trained on interpolation-completed labels acquire an over-smooth surface prior whose curvature statistics match the interpolation operator rather than true anatomy.

title: Label errors concentrate at pathology and low-contrast interfaces, so uniform-noise-robust training fails precisely where errors are clinically costly.
core_hypothesis: Real label error rate is a strong function of local image evidence (contrast, pathology presence), and methods tuned on uniform synthetic noise select for exactly the wrong robustness mechanism.

title: Training on raw per-rater masks as separate supervision samples yields calibrated boundary uncertainty for free, beating post-hoc uncertainty methods.
core_hypothesis: A vanilla segmentation network trained on unfused per-rater masks converges to the empirical rater distribution at boundaries, providing spatial uncertainty that matches held-out rater disagreement better than ensembles or MC-dropout applied to consensus-trained models.

title: Annotation guidelines drift during a labeling campaign, so early versus late cases in one dataset differ systematically and are temporally decodable.
core_hypothesis: Within a single dataset, annotation date (or case index as its proxy) predicts systematic mask differences, and models fit an average of shifting conventions rather than a single labeling function.

title: Much boundary disagreement is ontological, not perceptual: raters disagree about anatomical definitions, and per-region definition-ambiguity maps predict where all models plateau.
core_hypothesis: For structures with fuzzy anatomical definitions (organ boundaries at hila, vessel entry zones, gland tails), disagreement persists at high image quality, and these definitional zones form a fixed spatial map where every model's error saturates.

title: Annotators systematically under-include ambiguous voxels, so trained models inherit an undersegmentation bias fixable by a global bias correction rather than new architectures.
core_hypothesis: Reference masks are biased small relative to consensus-of-many, models replicate this bias, and a single learned isotropic boundary offset per structure removes most volumetric error for volumetry applications.

title: Quality-control passes smooth reference contours, deleting real high-frequency anatomy, so models are penalized for correctly predicting fine detail.
core_hypothesis: Post-QC masks have systematically lower surface frequency content than pre-QC raw annotations, and evaluation against post-QC masks ranks detail-preserving models below over-smoothing models.

title: Networks fit boundary label noise late in training and interior evidence early, so per-structure early stopping at different epochs beats a single global stopping point.
core_hypothesis: Learning is spatially staged: interior voxels are fit early and generalize, boundary-noise voxels are memorized late; the optimal stopping epoch therefore differs per structure according to its boundary ambiguity.

title: Dice is size-confounded: cross-method rankings flip when stratified by structure volume, and most claimed gains are small-structure operating-point changes.
core_hypothesis: A large fraction of reported improvements reduce to shifting the sensitivity-precision operating point on small structures, which stratified analysis and a matched-threshold comparison would reveal as non-improvements in shape recovery.

title: For radiotherapy organs-at-risk, dose-based evaluation reorders segmentation models relative to Dice, so geometric metrics are not valid surrogates for treatment impact.
core_hypothesis: Rank correlation between Dice-based and dose-metric-based model orderings is weak for organs near steep dose gradients, meaning model selection by Dice regularly picks dosimetrically inferior models.

title: Mean-over-cases Dice hides bimodal failure: catastrophic-failure rate is the clinically relevant statistic and is nearly uncorrelated with mean Dice among top methods.
core_hypothesis: Among methods within a few Dice points of each other, per-case failure-rate (fraction of cases below a usability threshold) varies severalfold and is statistically independent of the mean, so mean-based selection does not select the safest model.

title: Conventions for scoring empty or absent structures silently decide benchmark winners, and recomputing leaderboards under alternative conventions reorders the top entries.
core_hypothesis: For benchmarks containing absent-structure cases, the choice among standard empty-case conventions changes aggregate scores enough to permute top-five rankings, meaning some published orderings are artifacts of a bookkeeping decision.

title: Surface Dice with fixed tolerance is blind to uniform boundary bias: a model can score near-perfectly while being consistently offset inward by a margin-relevant amount.
core_hypothesis: Among models with equal surface Dice at clinical tolerance, signed boundary bias varies widely, and bias, not tolerance-band agreement, predicts volumetric and margin errors downstream.

title: Typical medical segmentation test sets are statistically underpowered to distinguish methods separated by the deltas the literature reports.
core_hypothesis: Under realistic per-case variance, the minimal detectable difference at conventional power on standard-size test sets exceeds a large fraction of published between-method gaps, so many reported orderings are statistically unresolved.

title: Topology-correctness should be the primary metric for tubular anatomy because Dice-superior models routinely break vessel and airway continuity that downstream navigation requires.
core_hypothesis: Overlap and topology quality are decoupled across models: within the top Dice cluster, connectivity-error counts vary by large factors, and the Dice-best model is often topology-worse, making Dice-based selection harmful for tubular structures.

title: The same Dice value denotes different segmentation quality across resolutions and structure scales, making cross-dataset and cross-modality comparisons systematically misleading.
core_hypothesis: A resolution-and-shape-normalized transformation of Dice (an effective boundary-error thickness) makes cross-dataset model comparisons consistent, and applying it retroactively changes conclusions about which modality or dataset is harder.

title: Evaluating on pre-cropped regions of interest inflates reported performance, and whole-scan evaluation including localization reorders methods.
core_hypothesis: Localization failure, not delineation failure, dominates whole-scan error for small structures, so methods optimized and ranked under oracle crops are misranked for deployment.

title: Medical segmentation models are texture-first, position-second, shape-last, inverting the anatomy-prior story used to motivate architecture design.
core_hypothesis: Controlled cue-conflict volumes (texture of organ A in the silhouette of organ B, at position of A or B) will show segmentation follows texture and position and largely ignores global shape.

title: Organ segmentation relies on absolute position in the volume so strongly that synthetic organ displacement breaks segmentation more than removing the organ's internal contrast.
core_hypothesis: Trained multi-organ models weight location priors over appearance: a normal-appearing organ at an unusual position is missed, while a contrast-flattened organ at the expected position is still segmented.

title: Segmentation networks do not exploit left-right anatomical symmetry, forgoing a constraint human readers use constantly.
core_hypothesis: Occluding or corrupting the contralateral side changes paired-organ segmentation negligibly, demonstrating that models process each side independently and ignore symmetry evidence that helps disambiguate pathology from anatomy.

title: Organ boundaries are inferred more from neighboring structures than from the organ's own edge contrast, so context corruption transfers errors across organs.
core_hypothesis: For low-contrast organs, occluding adjacent anchor structures degrades target segmentation more than degrading the target's own boundary contrast, and errors in one organ's segmentation predict correlated errors in its neighbors.

title: Scanner-conditional performance differences persist after intensity harmonization because models key on reconstruction-kernel texture, not intensity distributions.
core_hypothesis: The dominant learnable scanner fingerprint lives in local noise texture and edge response; models exploit it, and harmonizing intensities while leaving texture intact leaves the cross-scanner gap largely unchanged.

title: Organ models trained on mostly healthy anatomy actively inpaint lesions away rather than failing randomly, following a learned healthy-anatomy prior.
core_hypothesis: The failure is generative in character: models complete the organ as if healthy, smoothly interpolating over lesions and reproducing plausible-but-wrong boundaries, which is more dangerous than noisy failure because it looks credible.

title: For most organs, 3D context only matters within a thin band near through-plane boundaries, so full-3D models spend their compute on a few percent of voxels.
core_hypothesis: Voxelwise disagreement between matched 2D and 3D models concentrates in a narrow band at surfaces nearly parallel to the slicing plane, implying a hybrid that applies 3D reasoning only in that band matches full-3D accuracy at a fraction of the cost.

title: 3D transformer segmentation models have effective receptive fields that collapse to local neighborhoods, contradicting the long-range-context motivation for their use.
core_hypothesis: After training on standard medical datasets, attention-based volumetric models make decisions from effectively local evidence: perturbing or masking voxels beyond a small radius changes almost no predictions, matching CNN behavior.

title: CT models exploit absolute HU values as a shortcut, making them fragile to small calibration shifts that human readers absorb without noticing.
core_hypothesis: Segmentation decisions for low-contrast soft-tissue boundaries depend on absolute HU with near-threshold behavior; global shifts within plausible calibration tolerance produce disproportionate, spatially structured errors.

title: Because MR intensities are uncalibrated, MR-trained models are forced into geometry-reliant strategies and transfer shape knowledge across domains better than CT-trained models.
core_hypothesis: Absence of absolute intensity meaning in MR acts as an implicit regularizer against intensity shortcuts, so MR-trained encoders encode more geometry and transfer better to intensity-mismatched targets than CT-trained encoders of matched performance.

title: Segmentation models produce confident organ masks on anatomically impossible inputs, revealing the absence of any global anatomical sanity check.
core_hypothesis: On shuffled-organ, duplicated-organ, or physically impossible composite volumes, standard models emit high-confidence, well-formed masks, and no internal signal distinguishes these outputs from valid ones, implying anatomical plausibility is not represented.

title: Fractional partial-volume-aware labels would leave Dice unchanged but substantially improve derived volumetry, exposing binary masks as the wrong output space at medical resolutions.
core_hypothesis: Training on fractional-membership targets (from high-resolution references or mixture modeling) yields near-identical overlap metrics but significantly more accurate and less biased volume and surface estimates than binary training.

title: Resampling anisotropic volumes to isotropic grids destroys information irrecoverably, and native-grid models with anisotropy-aware operators beat resample-then-segment pipelines.
core_hypothesis: Interpolation to isotropic grids both hallucinates and averages away boundary evidence; operating natively with spacing-aware convolutions or attention preserves decisions that resampling forecloses, especially at through-plane boundaries.

title: Super-resolving thick-slice data before segmentation produces confidently hallucinated boundaries biased toward smooth anatomy, worse for safety than honest low-resolution uncertainty.
core_hypothesis: SR-then-segment pipelines transfer the SR prior into boundary placement: errors become systematically biased toward smooth, typical anatomy with reduced apparent uncertainty, degrading exactly the atypical cases while looking better on typical ones.

title: Patch-based training makes global constraints unlearnable in principle, and this, not architecture, is the root cause of topology and count errors in volumetric segmentation.
core_hypothesis: Errors violating whole-structure properties (connectivity, uniqueness, closed surfaces, volume conservation) are predominantly artifacts of patchwise objectives; brief full-volume fine-tuning at low resolution reduces them disproportionately compared to any patch-level intervention.

title: Sliding-window inference leaves grid-aligned artifacts, and part of what is reported as model uncertainty is actually window-placement variance.
core_hypothesis: Prediction differences under shifted window grids are substantial near window boundaries, correlate with reported uncertainty maps, and grid-shift ensembling both removes artifacts and reveals that some published uncertainty signal is inference-protocol variance.

title: Models exploit cropping and padding conventions as implicit coordinate encodings, so changing the crop convention at test time silently degrades performance.
core_hypothesis: Zero-padding and consistent cropping act as positional side channels; models trained under one framing convention rely on it, and deployment pipelines with different framing induce errors unexplained by image content.

title: Models trained on axially acquired and annotated data underperform on reformatted orientations even after isotropic resampling, because acquisition and annotation biases align with the axial plane.
core_hypothesis: There exists a residual axial-plane advantage in trained models that persists on isotropic data, caused jointly by slice-direction noise structure and in-plane annotation, and reformat-based label augmentation reduces it.

title: The adult-to-pediatric performance gap in organ segmentation is dominated by scale, not appearance, and pure geometric rescaling recovers most of it.
core_hypothesis: The primary failure axis is metric scale mismatch relative to the training distribution; size-normalizing inputs (physical rescaling to adult-equivalent organ scale) recovers the majority of the gap without any pediatric training data.

title: Field-of-view truncation is a larger real-world robustness threat than intensity shift, and truncation augmentation beats intensity augmentation for clinical variation.
core_hypothesis: Model behavior on FOV-truncated structures is erratic and bimodal (confident completion or total omission), truncation cases contribute disproportionately to deployment failures, and simple truncation augmentation yields larger real-world robustness gains than standard intensity augmentation.

title: Cross-site performance drops track case-mix and disease-prevalence differences more than scanner differences, so much of the reported domain gap is prevalence shift in disguise.
core_hypothesis: Reweighting or matching target-site cases to the source case-mix (by pathology burden, size, demographics) explains the majority of the cross-site segmentation gap for most organ tasks, leaving a small residual attributable to acquisition.

title: Intensity harmonization can remove the pathological contrast that lesion segmentation depends on, improving cross-site organ metrics while degrading pathology detection.
core_hypothesis: There is a measurable trade-off: harmonization strength correlates positively with cross-site organ segmentation consistency and negatively with lesion segmentation sensitivity, with popular methods already past the harm threshold for subtle lesions.

title: Multi-site pooled training plateaus because site-specific labeling protocols conflict, and per-site label heads outperform naive pooling, revealing label shift masquerading as image shift.
core_hypothesis: Sites define systematically different labeling functions for the same anatomy; pooled training forces one network to average incompatible targets, and a shared encoder with per-site decoding heads (or label-convention conditioning) outperforms pooled training on every site simultaneously.

title: Contrast-phase variation explains more cross-dataset variance in abdominal CT segmentation than scanner vendor, making phase-conditioning a cheap, ignored fix.
core_hypothesis: Variance decomposition of segmentation error across datasets attributes more to contrast phase than to vendor or protocol, and either phase-conditioning or phase-balanced training removes most of the phase-attributable error.

title: Segmentation accuracy is systematically stratified by patient body habitus, and geometric body-size normalization closes gaps that intensity-based domain adaptation cannot.
core_hypothesis: Models encode training-population habitus priors; performance declines monotonically toward both habitus extremes, and a geometric normalization of body cross-section removes more of this than intensity harmonization, showing the effect is spatial-prior driven.

title: Deployment performance does not decay smoothly with protocol change but cliffs at specific parameter thresholds, so mapping cliffs is more useful than optimizing average robustness.
core_hypothesis: Model performance as a function of continuous acquisition parameters (dose, kernel sharpness, slice thickness, echo time) exhibits identifiable discontinuity-like transitions, stable across cases, defining a safe operating envelope that average-robustness metrics cannot express.

title: Lesion segmentation progress is dominated by detection, not delineation: decomposing Dice shows delineation is near-saturated and methods differ almost entirely in which lesions they find.
core_hypothesis: Across published lesion methods, variance in detection-conditional delineation quality is small, while variance in lesion-level detection is large, meaning the field is unknowingly doing detection research with a segmentation metric.

title: Models are wildly inconsistent at counting lesions across same-patient adjacent timepoints, an instability invisible to Dice but fatal for longitudinal clinical use.
core_hypothesis: Lesion-count and lesion-identity consistency of independent per-timepoint segmentation is far worse than within-scan noise justifies: small acquisition differences flip detections near threshold, making count changes mostly artifactual.

title: The minimum detectable lesion size of a pipeline is set implicitly by loss weighting, not resolution, and can be dialed predictably, meaning current pipelines choose a clinical sensitivity threshold by accident.
core_hypothesis: There is a monotone, quantifiable mapping from loss size-weighting parameters to the lesion-size sensitivity curve, stable across datasets, so the detection threshold is a controllable design parameter with a measurable precision trade-off.

title: Binary masks are the wrong output space for infiltrative disease: continuous involvement fields match multi-rater behavior and longitudinal biology better than forced hard boundaries.
core_hypothesis: Rater disagreement on infiltrative margins is structured and graded, consistent with raters thresholding a shared continuous involvement percept at different operating points; predicting the continuous field directly explains multi-rater data with fewer assumptions and yields more stable longitudinal measures.

title: Lesion models exploit acquisition-indication cues, effectively learning why the scan was taken, which inflates retrospective benchmarks and collapses on screening populations.
core_hypothesis: Part of measured lesion-segmentation performance derives from indication-correlated acquisition features rather than lesion appearance, so performance drops sharply on indication-mismatched populations (screening or incidental settings) beyond what image quality explains.

title: Models learn per-scan lesion-count priors from dataset multiplicity statistics, hurting solitary-lesion cases and inventing company for lonely lesions.
core_hypothesis: Detection decisions are not conditionally independent given local evidence: finding one lesion changes the model's propensity elsewhere in the scan, matching training multiplicity statistics, which manifests as false positives on solitary-lesion cases and misses on unusually-many-lesion cases.

title: For treatment-response assessment, consistent bias beats inconsistent accuracy: a lower-Dice model with stable errors classifies response better than a higher-Dice model with variable errors.
core_hypothesis: Between-timepoint error correlation varies widely across models and dominates change-detection accuracy, so cross-sectional Dice ranking is a poor and sometimes inverted predictor of response-classification performance.

title: Clinicians correct AI-drawn contours less than identical errors drawn by humans, so clinical contour distributions drift toward model biases after AI adoption.
core_hypothesis: For matched error magnitude and type, edit probability and edit extent are lower when errors originate from an AI proposal than from a human colleague's contour, and post-adoption institutional contour statistics measurably shift toward the deployed model's systematic biases.

title: Correction time depends on error topology, not error volume, so optimizing models for editability rather than Dice changes which model is best for clinical workflows.
core_hypothesis: An edit-cost model based on error topology (component count, slice dispersion, boundary coherence) predicts correction time far better than Dice or volume error, and model rankings under predicted edit cost differ from Dice rankings.

title: Interactive segmentation models waste clicks because they model where users click as noise, though click sequences follow predictable clinical attention patterns.
core_hypothesis: Real clinical click sequences are predictable from image and task context; training interactive models against realistic click policies rather than random simulation reduces clicks-to-acceptance substantially at fixed model capacity.

title: AI contouring homogenizes inter-clinician variability, which reduces the statistical sensitivity of clinical endpoints and quality metrics built on natural contour diversity.
core_hypothesis: Post-AI contour distributions collapse toward the model mode, breaking variance assumptions in consensus algorithms, inter-observer QA statistics, and trial endpoints, in measurable ways that can produce false confidence and missed protocol deviations.

title: Near-perfect automation degrades human review quality so much that intermediate-accuracy models can yield better final corrected contours than the best models.
core_hypothesis: Reviewer error-detection probability falls as model error rate falls (rare errors get missed), so final-output quality as a function of model accuracy is non-monotone, with a regime where better models produce worse clinically finalized contours.

title: Humans cannot identify which AI contours contain clinically significant errors when the errors are smooth and anatomically plausible, dissociating plausibility from correctness.
core_hypothesis: Reader detection of AI contour errors depends on plausibility violations rather than on error magnitude, so smooth systematic errors of clinically significant size evade detection at near-chance rates, while trivial jagged artifacts get flagged.

title: Quality-assurance models should predict where clinicians would edit, not where Dice is lost; the two targets diverge and the edit-prediction target generalizes better.
core_hypothesis: Edit events are a distinct, partially disjoint signal from geometric error, dominated by clinical salience; QA models trained on edit logs identify actionable problems with higher precision and transfer across sites better than error-regression QA models.

title: Merging partially labeled datasets teaches models to suppress specific organs conditioned on dataset fingerprints, a structured bias rather than random noise.
core_hypothesis: Networks resolve the label conflict by learning dataset-identity features and conditionally suppressing organs that were unlabeled in the inferred source, so suppression follows the fingerprint, not the anatomy, and reactivates when fingerprints are removed.

title: Iterated self-training on unlabeled medical volumes collapses shape diversity toward atlas-like average anatomy, quantifiable as shrinking shape-space variance per iteration.
core_hypothesis: Each self-training round smooths predictions toward high-prior shapes, so the predicted shape distribution contracts (variance loss, mode collapse toward typical anatomy), degrading rare-variant performance while average Dice appears stable or improved.

title: Dense 3D labels are mostly redundant: a labeling-budget scaling law shows a few well-chosen slices per volume achieve most of full-annotation performance across organs.
core_hypothesis: Performance as a function of labeled-slice fraction follows a sharply saturating curve whose saturation point is predictable from structure geometry (surface-to-volume ratio and inter-slice correlation), enabling principled budget allocation across structures and cases.

title: The efficiency ranking of annotation modes (scribbles, boundary tracing, clicks) inverts with structure geometry, so efficient-annotation guidance must be structure-conditional.
core_hypothesis: Per-unit-time model improvement from each annotation mode depends on structure geometry: scribbles win for large compact organs, boundary tracing wins for thin or sheet-like structures, and the crossover is predictable, making mode selection a solvable assignment problem.

title: A label-free anatomical-consistency battery (containment, adjacency, volume ratios, symmetry) predicts model ranking on unseen sites, enabling annotation-free local model selection.
core_hypothesis: Violation rates of hard anatomical invariants computed on unlabeled local scans correlate strongly with labeled accuracy rank, because the same failure processes produce both invariant violations and boundary errors.

title: Atlas-propagated training labels imprint the registration regularizer into segmentation networks, creating direction-dependent boundary bias that survives training.
core_hypothesis: Smoothness-regularized registration under-deforms into thin protrusions and over-smooths concavities, so propagated labels carry signed geometric bias, and networks trained on them reproduce the registration's characteristic error signature even on structures where direct annotation exists.

title: Measured inter-rater variance predicts each task's data-scaling saturation point, giving an a priori sample-size calculator for segmentation dataset construction.
core_hypothesis: Data-scaling curves for segmentation saturate when model-reference disagreement approaches the rater-noise floor, so a small pilot multi-rater study measuring that floor predicts the useful dataset size before large-scale annotation begins.

title: Voxelwise confidence is spatially miscalibrated in a fixed pattern (overconfident at boundaries, underconfident in interiors), and a distance-to-boundary recalibration outperforms expensive uncertainty methods.
core_hypothesis: Miscalibration is primarily a deterministic function of distance to the predicted boundary, stable across cases and datasets for a given model family, so a one-dimensional recalibration map fixes most of it without ensembles or sampling.

title: Ensemble disagreement in medical segmentation localizes label noise rather than model uncertainty, making ensembles accidental annotation-error detectors.
core_hypothesis: Voxels of high cross-member disagreement coincide predominantly with reference-label errors and inter-rater ambiguity zones rather than with model-knowledge gaps, so ensemble disagreement is better used for label auditing than for flagging model unreliability.

title: Calibration degrades faster than accuracy under site shift, so confidence-based triage becomes unsafe exactly in the deployment settings it exists for.
core_hypothesis: Under increasing site shift, calibration error grows disproportionately relative to accuracy loss, and specifically in the overconfident direction, so fixed-confidence auto-accept thresholds admit rising error rates that the system cannot see.

title: Abstention mechanisms in medical segmentation preferentially reject pathological cases, converting selective prediction into a care-disparity engine.
core_hypothesis: Because pathology increases predictive uncertainty, abstention correlates with disease burden, so the auto-processed stream is enriched for healthy anatomy while sick patients are disproportionately deferred, undermining both the clinical value and the equity of automation.

title: Voxelwise conformal prediction yields clinically useless margins, but structure-level conformal objects (volume intervals, boundary bands) are usable and transfer across organs.
core_hypothesis: Guarantees should attach to clinical quantities: conformalizing derived scalars and boundary offsets yields tight, actionable sets, and the nonconformity geometry is similar enough across organs that calibration transfers with small correction, unlike voxelwise sets.

title: Displaying voxel-uncertainty overlays misdirects clinician attention toward unimportant ambiguity and away from confident errors, degrading review outcomes.
core_hypothesis: Uncertainty overlays anchor reviewers to highlighted regions, increasing edits of clinically minor ambiguous boundaries while reducing detection of high-confidence systematic errors, so overlay-assisted review can produce worse final contours than unassisted review when model errors are confident.

title: Point prompts are ill-posed in medical images because anatomy is hierarchical: prompt ambiguity over nested structures explains most variance in promptable-model medical performance.
core_hypothesis: The dominant error source for promptable models on medical images is hierarchy-level misidentification, not delineation, so an explicit measure of nested-structure ambiguity at the prompt location predicts per-prompt failure probability across models.

title: Clicks required by 2D-native interactive models on volumes scale with slice count rather than shape complexity, a click-budget scaling law exposing the 3D economy failure.
core_hypothesis: For slice-wise interactive models, clicks-to-target-accuracy grows near-linearly with the number of occupied slices regardless of per-slice difficulty, whereas natively 3D interactive methods scale with shape complexity, so the crossover defines when 2D interactive tools are economically irrational for volumes.

title: Text-promptable medical segmentation inherits report-language bias: prompted with an organ name, models over-segment the clinically notable part rather than the anatomical extent.
core_hypothesis: Language-grounded segmentation models bind organ terms to the regions reports discuss (abnormal, enhancing, or symptomatic parts), producing systematic truncation of normal anatomy and inflation of abnormal regions relative to anatomically supervised models.

title: Deep features of generalist vision models cluster medical images by modality and texture rather than anatomy, contradicting the assumption that generalist features encode what is depicted.
core_hypothesis: Representational similarity analysis on medical images will show late-layer generalist features dominated by acquisition attributes (modality, sequence, kernel) with anatomy decodable only weakly and mainly from mid-level layers, implying adaptation should graft onto mid-level features rather than fine-tune from the top.

title: Zero-shot foundation-model segmentation quality on medical structures is largely predicted by a simple boundary-contrast statistic, so much of medical adaptation gain is concentrated where contrast is low.
core_hypothesis: A per-structure boundary-contrast measure explains the majority of zero-shot performance variance across anatomical structures, implying foundation models already handle high-contrast medical anatomy and adaptation research should be evaluated specifically on the low-contrast residual.

title: Topology errors are driven by acquisition noise, not model choice: the same model produces different topology on same-patient rescans, so topology losses treat the wrong cause.
core_hypothesis: Topology of thin-structure segmentations is chaotic with respect to input noise: test-retest inputs flip connectivity decisions at weak-evidence points, and this input-driven variance exceeds between-model topology differences, implying stabilization (multi-acquisition fusion, evidence accumulation) beats topology-penalized training.

title: Below a resolvability threshold, vessel and airway models hallucinate continuity from learned priors, drawing through real gaps and fabricating clinical patency.
core_hypothesis: Models trained with continuity-favoring supervision cannot distinguish resolution-limited apparent gaps from true occlusions, and systematically bridge both, so their outputs are anti-informative exactly for occlusive disease, with the bridging rate a function of an SNR-diameter product.

title: Shape-prior models trade rare-anatomy accuracy for average-case smoothness, making anatomical variants a predictable casualty of prior-constrained segmentation.
core_hypothesis: The stronger the shape prior, the larger the performance penalty on statistically rare but real anatomy (horseshoe kidney, situs anomalies, resections), with prior-free models degrading more gracefully, so prior strength is a hidden fairness parameter over anatomical minorities.

title: Mask-to-mesh conversion introduces geometric bias comparable to model error for small structures, so downstream planning error is misattributed to networks.
core_hypothesis: Standard iso-surfacing and smoothing pipelines add systematic volume and curvature bias that, for structures below a size threshold, rivals or exceeds the upstream model's boundary error, so end-to-end geometric accuracy is pipeline-limited, not model-limited.

title: For scalar clinical endpoints, direct image-to-measurement regression beats segment-then-measure in accuracy and robustness, questioning segmentation's role as a universal intermediate.
core_hypothesis: The segmentation intermediate adds error and fragility for scalar endpoints: direct regression trained on measurement labels achieves lower measurement error and degrades more gracefully under domain shift, because it needs not solve the harder full-delineation problem.

title: Detecting surgical absence is a distinct capability from segmenting presence: models confidently hallucinate removed organs, and presence-trained models cannot learn absence from ordinary data.
core_hypothesis: Absence is not the low-confidence tail of presence: models produce well-formed organ masks at post-resection sites using contextual priors, and absence recognition requires dedicated negative supervision or explicit reasoning, not more presence data.

title: Dice loss causes calibration collapse by construction because it optimizes a set statistic, and the community's default compound loss inherits the damage.
core_hypothesis: Optimizing set-overlap statistics drives probabilities toward saturation independent of evidence strength, so the standard compound loss produces near-binary confidence; sequenced training (cross-entropy convergence, then brief Dice fine-tuning) preserves accuracy while retaining most calibration, showing the trade-off is schedulable rather than fundamental.

title: Heavy augmentation in medical pipelines works mainly as label-noise regularization, not domain robustness, and boundary-targeted label smoothing recovers most of its benefit.
core_hypothesis: A large share of augmentation's benefit comes from preventing memorization of noisy boundary labels (by decoupling boundary voxels from exact positions), so replacing heavy augmentation with boundary-band label smoothing recovers most in-domain and part of cross-domain benefit at far lower compute.
